definition_en: an amount left over after what is needed has been used
core_image: 仓库里堆着多出来的粮食袋，标签写着剩余
scene: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
sceneCN: 这里 surplus 是「剩余」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

senses.title: An amount left over
senses.definition: an amount that remains after needs are met
senses.definitionCN: 满足需求后剩下的数量
senses.example: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of something left over.
senses.whyCN: 这是「剩下之物」的基本义项。

senses.title: A financial gain
senses.definition: the amount by which income is greater than spending
senses.definitionCN: 收入大于支出的部分
senses.example: The government reported a budget surplus.
senses.exampleCN: 政府报告了预算盈余。
senses.why: In finance the leftover becomes a positive balance.
senses.whyCN: 在财政中，剩余变成正结余。

intro.en: Surplus joins the Latin words for above and more.
intro.cn: surplus 把拉丁语中表示「在上」和「更多」的词结合起来。

items.en: Surplus named an amount left over.
Surplus extended to budget and trade balances.
items.cn: surplus 扩展到预算与贸易结余。

note.en: Surplus is compared with look-alike words and with words for extra amounts.
note.cn: 把 surplus 与形近词以及表示多余数量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surplus is what remains above what was needed.
normalIntro.cn: surplus 是超出所需而剩下的部分。

normal.en: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
normal.cn: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

normal.en: The government reported a budget surplus.
normal.cn: 政府报告了预算盈余。

normal.en: The country runs a trade surplus with its neighbours.

normal.en: Surplus goods were stored in the old barn.
normal.cn: 剩余物资存放在旧谷仓里。

normal.en: A surplus of teachers filled the hall.
normal.cn: 多余的教师挤满了大厅。

abstract.en: Surplus is the quiet proof that a system produced more than it needed.
abstract.cn: 剩余是一个体系产出多于所需的无声证明。

abstract.en: What is extra for one place may be missing in another.
abstract.cn: 对一地多余的东西，在另一地可能正缺。

abstract.en: The word adds plus to super and turns abundance into a quantity.
abstract.cn: 这个词把 plus 加到 super 上，把丰足变成一个数量。

dict_mnemonic.text: super 表示「超过」，plus 表示「更多」，surplus 就是多出来的部分，即剩余、盈余。

root: 源自拉丁语 super（在上）与 plus（更多），经古法语 surplus 进入英语，指超出所需的部分。

sensesIntro.en: Surplus means an amount left over, or a positive balance of income over spending.
sensesIntro.cn: surplus 指剩余数量，也指收入大于支出的盈余。

core.en: More than the need, left in hand.
core.cn: 多于所需而留在手里的部分。

branches.en: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
branches.cn: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

branches.en: Surplus goods were stored in the old barn.
branches.cn: 剩余物资存放在旧谷仓里。

branches.en: The government reported a budget surplus.

branches.en: Corn left over and money left over share one word.

branches.cn: 该国与邻国保持贸易顺差。

intro.en: Surplus forms surpluses and relates to plus and super.
intro.cn: surplus 可构成复数 surpluses，并与 plus、super 相关。

latinIntro.en: Latin super and plus both survive in English as separate words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 与 plus 都作为独立词留在英语中。

items.exampleCN: super 在拉丁语中意为在上。

definition_en: an unexpected event or feeling, or to cause that feeling
core_image: 打开盒子的一瞬间，人们露出吃惊的表情
scene: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。His answer caused great surprise.
sceneCN: 这里 surprise 是「惊讶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的回答让大家十分惊讶。

senses.title: The feeling of shock
senses.definition: the feeling caused by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 由意外之事引起的感受
senses.example: His answer caused great surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让大家十分惊讶。
senses.why: This is the core feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情绪义项。

senses.title: An unexpected event
senses.definition: something that happens without being expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有预料到而发生的事
senses.example: The party was a complete surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这场聚会完全是个惊喜。
senses.why: Here the word names the event, not the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里指事件而非感受。

senses.title: To cause surprise
senses.definition: to make someone feel sudden wonder
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到突然的惊奇
senses.example: The news surprised everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让房间里所有人都感到惊讶。
senses.why: As a verb it names the act of causing the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时指引发这种感受。

intro.en: Surprise came from a French verb meaning to overtake suddenly.
intro.cn: surprise 来自一个意为「突然赶上」的法语动词。

items.en: Surprise came to mean sudden wonder.
items.cn: surprise 转而表示突然的惊奇。

note.en: Surprise is compared with look-alike sur- words and with words for wonder.
note.cn: 把 surprise 与形近的 sur- 词以及表示惊奇的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surprise moves from sudden seizure to sudden wonder.
normalIntro.cn: surprise 从突然抓住演变为突然惊奇。

normal.en: His answer caused great surprise.

abstract.cn: 当世界跑得比计划快时，惊讶就发生了。

abstract.en: The word once meant a sudden attack, which is also a kind of surprise.

abstract.en: A surprise interrupts time for a moment.

core.en: Being caught by what we did not expect.

definition_zh: 出奇地；令人惊讶地；出乎意料地
definition_en: in a way that is unexpected or causes surprise
core_image: 一个难题旁画着对勾，答题者自己都不敢相信
scene: 这次考试出奇地容易。The test was surprisingly easy for everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 surprisingly 是「出乎意料地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这次考试出奇地容易。

senses.title: In an unexpected way
senses.definition: in a way that is not expected
senses.definitionCN: 以没有预料到的方式
senses.example: The test was surprisingly easy for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试对每个人来说都出奇地容易。
senses.why: This is the core sense of unexpectedness.
senses.whyCN: 这是「出乎意料」的核心义项。

senses.title: Used to comment on a whole sentence
senses.definition: used to say that a fact is surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某个事实令人惊讶
senses.example: Surprisingly, nobody noticed the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 令人惊讶的是，没有人发现这个错误。
senses.why: As a sentence adverb it comments on the whole statement.
senses.whyCN: 作句子副词时评论整个陈述。

intro.en: Surprisingly adds two endings to the verb surprise.
intro.cn: surprisingly 在动词 surprise 后加了两个词尾。

items.en: Surprisingly became a common adverb of comment.
items.cn: surprisingly 成为常见的评论副词。

note.en: Surprisingly is compared with its word family and with other comment adverbs.

normalIntro.en: Surprisingly marks what breaks an expectation.

normal.en: Surprisingly, nobody noticed the mistake.
normal.cn: 令人惊讶的是，没有人发现这个错误。

normal.en: The old car ran surprisingly well.

abstract.en: Surprisingly measures the distance between expectation and fact.
abstract.cn: surprisingly 衡量预期与事实之间的距离。

abstract.en: The adverb turns a plain sentence into a small raised eyebrow.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把平铺直叙变成轻轻挑眉。

abstract.en: What is surprising today becomes ordinary tomorrow.

sensesIntro.en: Surprisingly means in an unexpected way, or comments that a fact is surprising.

definition_en: to stop fighting and give up, or to hand something over

scene: 被围困的士兵最终选择投降。The surrounded soldiers finally chose to surrender.
sceneCN: 这里 surrender 是「投降」（第 1 个义项）；句意：被围困的士兵最终选择投降。

senses.title: To stop fighting
senses.definition: to admit defeat and stop fighting
senses.definitionCN: 承认失败并停止战斗
senses.example: The surrounded soldiers finally chose to surrender.
senses.exampleCN: 被围困的士兵最终选择投降。
senses.why: This is the military core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是军事上的核心义项。

senses.title: To give something up
senses.definition: to hand over something one has
senses.definitionCN: 交出自己所拥有的东西
senses.example: They surrendered their passports at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在边境交出了护照。
senses.why: Here the word means handing over rather than military defeat.
senses.whyCN: 这里指交出而非军事失败。

senses.title: To yield to a feeling
senses.definition: to stop resisting an emotion or desire
senses.definitionCN: 不再抵抗某种情感或欲望
senses.example: She surrendered to a wave of tiredness.
senses.exampleCN: 她屈服于一阵疲倦。
senses.why: The sense extends from battle to inner struggle.
senses.whyCN: 该义从战斗延伸到内心挣扎。

intro.en: Surrender means to give back, from French sur and rendre.
intro.cn: surrender 意为交还，来自法语的 sur 与 rendre。

items.en: Surrender became the standard word for giving up a fight.
items.cn: surrender 成为表示停止战斗的标准词。

note.en: Surrender is compared with look-alike sur- words and with words for yielding.
note.cn: 把 surrender 与形近的 sur- 词以及表示屈服的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surrender is the act of handing over what one held.
normalIntro.cn: surrender 是交出自己所持之物的动作。

abstract.en: Surrender is a decision made when fighting no longer serves life.
abstract.cn: 投降是当战斗不再服务于生命时作出的决定。

abstract.en: To surrender something can be strength rather than weakness.
abstract.cn: 交出某物可以是力量而非软弱。

abstract.en: The word gives back what was taken, in name and in deed.
abstract.cn: 这个词在名与实上把取走的东西交还。

examples.en: The surrounded soldiers finally chose to surrender.

definition_en: to be or go all around something
core_image: 一圈高大的树把平静的小湖围在中间
scene: 高高的树围绕着那座小湖。Tall trees surround the small lake.
sceneCN: 这里 surround 是「围绕」（第 1 个义项）；句意：高高的树围绕着那座小湖。

senses.title: To be all around
senses.definition: to be placed all around something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物四周

senses.title: To close in on

senses.title: To be closely connected with

senses.example: Mystery surrounds the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子笼罩着神秘色彩。
senses.why: The spatial image extends to atmosphere and circumstance.
senses.whyCN: 空间意象延伸到氛围与境况。

definition_en: the things and conditions around a person or place

scene: 这座小城周围的环境非常安静。The surroundings of the small town are very quiet.

senses.title: The area around a place

senses.title: The conditions of daily life

definition_en: a study of opinions or facts, or to look over an area
core_image: 研究员拿着问卷站在街角，记录路人的回答
scene: 研究者调查了五百名居民。The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
sceneCN: 这里 survey 是「调查」（第 1 个义项）；句意：研究者调查了五百名居民。

senses.title: A study of opinions
senses.definition: a set of questions used to collect opinions or facts
senses.definitionCN: 用于收集意见或事实的一组问题
senses.example: The researchers surveyed five hundred residents.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者调查了五百名居民。
senses.why: This is the common social-science sense.

senses.title: The measuring of land
senses.definition: the act of measuring land or an area

senses.example: They surveyed the land before building.

senses.title: A general view

senses.example: The book gives a survey of modern art.

senses.why: Here the word means looking over the whole.

senses.title: To stay alive
senses.definition: to continue to live, especially in difficult conditions
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在困境中继续活着
senses.example: Only a few plants can survive in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数植物能在沙漠中存活。
senses.why: This is the core sense of staying alive.

senses.title: To live through danger

senses.exampleCN: 她在事故中幸存，没有受重伤。

senses.title: To outlive someone

examples.cn: 她在事故中幸存，没有受重伤。

core.en: Life carried past a threat.

definition_en: a person who continues to live after danger or the death of others
core_image: 救援艇上裹着毯子的人，回头望向渐渐平静的海面
scene: 救援队找到了唯一的幸存者。The rescue team found the only survivor.
sceneCN: 这里 survivor 是「幸存者」（第 1 个义项）；句意：救援队找到了唯一的幸存者。

senses.title: A person who stays alive
senses.definition: someone who continues to live after danger
senses.definitionCN: 经历危险后仍然活着的人
senses.example: The rescue team found the only survivor.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队找到了唯一的幸存者。
senses.why: This is the basic personal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是指人的基本义项。

senses.title: A person who endures hardship
senses.definition: someone who continues after a hard experience
senses.definitionCN: 经历艰难之后仍继续生活的人
senses.example: She is a survivor of a long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一场长期疾病的幸存者。

senses.whyCN: 这里指疾病或艰难而非事故。

abstract.en: A survivor carries the memory of those who did not return.
abstract.cn: 幸存者承载着未能归来者的记忆。

abstract.en: The word names a person by what they passed through.
abstract.cn: 这个词用一个人所经历的事情来称呼他。

abstract.en: Surviving can be a duty as much as a gift.
abstract.cn: 幸存既可能是礼物，也可能是责任。

definition_en: to believe someone may be guilty, or a person thought to be guilty
core_image: 警探在灯下翻看档案，目光停在一个人名上
scene: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。The police suspect that he hid the money.
sceneCN: 这里 suspect 是「怀疑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。

senses.title: To believe someone is guilty
senses.definition: to think that someone may be guilty or dishonest
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人可能有罪或不诚实
senses.example: The police suspect that he hid the money.
senses.exampleCN: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。
senses.why: This is the core sense of suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 这是「怀疑」的核心义项。

senses.title: A person believed guilty
senses.definition: a person believed to have committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 被认为犯了罪的人
senses.example: The suspect was held for questioning.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑犯被拘留审问。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the person.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时指人。

senses.title: Likely to be bad or false
senses.definition: likely to be bad, false, or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 可能是坏的、假的或危险的
senses.example: They found a suspect package by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门边发现一个可疑包裹。
senses.why: As an adjective it describes things that raise doubt.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时描述引起怀疑的事物。

intro.en: Suspect comes from a Latin verb meaning to look up at with distrust.
intro.cn: suspect 来自一个意为「仰视并起疑」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Suspect became a verb and a noun.

note.en: Suspect is compared with look-alike words and with words for doubt.
note.cn: 把 suspect 与形近词以及表示怀疑的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Suspect links the act of doubting and the person doubted.
normalIntro.cn: suspect 把怀疑的动作与被怀疑的人联系起来。

normal.en: The police suspect that he hid the money.
normal.cn: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。

normal.en: The suspect was held for questioning.
normal.cn: 嫌疑犯被拘留审问。

normal.en: They found a suspect package by the door.
normal.cn: 他们在门边发现一个可疑包裹。

normal.en: I suspect the plan will fail.
normal.cn: 我怀疑这项计划会失败。

normal.en: She was suspected of taking the file.
normal.cn: 她被怀疑拿走了文件。

abstract.en: To suspect is to look at someone and see a hidden possibility.
abstract.cn: 怀疑就是看着某人并看见一种隐藏的可能。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a feeling to a person to a thing.
abstract.cn: 这个词轻易地从感觉转到人，再转到物。

abstract.en: Doubt can protect us, yet it can also wound the innocent.
abstract.cn: 怀疑能保护我们，也能伤害无辜者。

core.en: Seeing a hidden possibility in someone.

branches.en: The police suspect that he hid the money.
branches.cn: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。

branches.en: I suspect the plan will fail.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere（看）也出现在 inspect、respect 与 spectator 中。

definition_en: to stop or delay something, or to hang something from above
core_image: 钟摆从上方垂下，停在半空中
scene: 比赛因大雨暂停了。The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 suspend 是「暂停」（第 1 个义项）；句意：比赛因大雨暂停了。

senses.title: To stop temporarily
senses.definition: to stop something for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 使某事停止一段时间
senses.example: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因大雨暂停了。
senses.why: This is the common sense of a temporary stop.
senses.whyCN: 这是「暂时停止」的常见义项。

senses.title: To hang from above
senses.definition: to hang something so that it is held from above
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从上吊起
senses.example: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物理义项。

senses.title: To remove someone temporarily
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job or school for a time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人暂时离开工作或学校
senses.example: He was suspended from school for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他被停学一周。
senses.why: Here the stopping applies to a person's position.
senses.whyCN: 这里停止的是人的职位。

intro.en: Suspend joins Latin words for under and hanging.

normalIntro.cn: suspend 意为把某物吊起，或把某事按住。

abstract.en: Suspension is time held in the air before it falls again.
abstract.cn: 暂停是时间悬在空中，等待再次落下。

abstract.en: The same word holds a lamp and holds back a decision.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既吊着灯，也按住决定。

abstract.en: To suspend is to interrupt without ending.

definition_en: a feeling that someone may be guilty or something may be wrong
core_image: 一个人站在门口，透过半开的门缝向里张望

sceneCN: 这里 suspicion 是「怀疑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。

senses.title: A feeling of doubt
senses.definition: a feeling that something is wrong or someone is guilty
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某事不对或某人有罪的感觉
senses.example: His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。
senses.why: This is the core feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情绪义项。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a slight amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点
senses.example: There was a suspicion of a smile on her face.

intro.cn: suspicion 是拉丁语「怀疑」动词的名词形式。

items.en: Suspicion meant a feeling of doubt.
Suspicion named the state of doubting.
Suspicion also means a very small amount.
items.cn: suspicion 也表示极少的一点。

note.en: Suspicion is compared with look-alike words and with words for doubt.

abstract.en: A suspicion can grow from a word into a wall.

senses.title: Likely to be wrong
senses.definition: seeming likely to be illegal or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 看起来可能违法或危险的
senses.example: The strange package by the door looked suspicious.
senses.exampleCN: 门边的陌生包裹看起来很可疑。
senses.why: This is the common sense of a thing that raises doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这是「引起怀疑之物」的常见义项。

senses.title: Tending not to trust
senses.definition: feeling that people cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 觉得他人不可信任的
senses.example: He was suspicious of every offer of help.

definition_en: to keep something going, hold it up, or suffer an injury

definition_en: to make food or drink go down the throat, or to accept something hard
core_image: 一只燕子掠过水面，桌边的人咽下药片
scene: 他慢慢吞下那口苦药。He slowly swallowed the bitter medicine.

senses.title: To make something go down

senses.definitionCN: 不抗议地接受侮辱或损失
senses.example: She swallowed her anger and said nothing.

dict_mnemonic.note: 义项记忆 · 发誓 → 宣誓 → 咒骂
dict_mnemonic.text: swear 本义是郑重起誓，正式场合即「宣誓」，而愤怒时的誓言久而久之变成「咒骂」。

root: 来自古英语 swerian，源于日耳曼语 swaran（宣誓），核心是以言语郑重作保。

sensesIntro.en: Swear means to promise solemnly, to take a formal oath, or to speak rudely.
sensesIntro.cn: swear 指郑重发誓、正式宣誓，或粗鲁咒骂。

core.en: Words bound to honor.

branches.en: He swore to tell the truth in court.
branches.cn: 他在法庭上发誓说出真相。

branches.en: She swore never to return.
branches.cn: 她发誓再也不回来。

branches.en: The witness swore an oath before speaking.
branches.cn: 证人在发言前宣了誓。

branches.en: He swore loudly when he dropped the box.
branches.cn: 他摔落箱子时大声咒骂。

branches.en: A private promise and a public oath share one verb.
branches.cn: 私下承诺与公开宣誓共用一个动词。

intro.en: Swear forms swore, sworn, swearing, and the adjective sworn.
intro.cn: swear 可构成 swore、sworn、swearing 与形容词 sworn。

latinIntro.en: Swear is Germanic; Latin iurare, to swear, survives in jury and jurist.
latinIntro.cn: swear 属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 iurare（宣誓）仍留在 jury 与 jurist 中。

items.example: He swore to tell the truth.

latinEntries.example: Swerian is the Old English source of swear.
latinEntries.exampleCN: swerian 是 swear 的古英语来源。

definition_en: liquid that comes through the skin when one is hot, or to produce it
core_image: 长跑结束后，额头的汗珠沿着脸颊滑落
scene: 跑完长跑后，他满头是汗。After the long run, he was covered in sweat.
sceneCN: 这里 sweat 是「汗」（第 1 个义项）；句意：跑完长跑后，他满头是汗。

senses.title: Liquid from the skin
senses.definition: salty liquid that comes through the skin when one is hot
senses.definitionCN: 热时从皮肤渗出的咸味液体
senses.example: After the long run, he was covered in sweat.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完长跑后，他满头是汗。
senses.why: This is the basic bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的生理义项。

senses.title: To produce sweat
senses.definition: to give off sweat from the skin
senses.definitionCN: 从皮肤排出汗液
senses.example: The runners were sweating in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步者在太阳下出汗。
senses.why: As a verb it names the process.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时指这一过程。

senses.title: Hard work or worry
senses.definition: hard effort or anxious effort
senses.definitionCN: 艰苦的努力或焦虑
senses.example: She earned the prize with years of sweat.
senses.exampleCN: 她多年辛苦才赢得这个奖。
senses.why: The body's sign of effort becomes a metaphor for labor.
senses.whyCN: 身体用力的标志变成劳动的隐喻。

intro.en: Sweat is an old Germanic word for the body's moisture.
intro.cn: sweat 是表示身体湿气的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Sweat meant moisture from the body.
Sweater named a garment for warmth.

note.en: Sweat is compared with look-alike words and with words for body moisture.
note.cn: 把 sweat 与形近词以及表示身体湿气的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sweat is moisture, the act of making it, and the labor behind it.
normalIntro.cn: sweat 是汗水、出汗的动作，以及背后的辛苦。

normal.en: After the long run, he was covered in sweat.
normal.cn: 跑完长跑后，他满头是汗。

normal.en: The runners were sweating in the sun.
normal.cn: 跑步者在太阳下出汗。

normal.en: She earned the prize with years of sweat.
normal.cn: 她多年辛苦才赢得这个奖。

normal.en: He broke into a cold sweat before the test.
normal.cn: 考试前他冒了一身冷汗。

normal.en: The room was hot and sweat ran down his face.
normal.cn: 房间很热，汗水顺着他的脸流下。

abstract.en: Sweat is the body writing its effort on the skin.
abstract.cn: 汗水是身体把努力写在皮肤上。

abstract.en: The word makes labor visible and measurable.
abstract.cn: 这个词让劳动变得可见可量。

abstract.en: Fear can produce the same drops as running.
abstract.cn: 恐惧能产生与奔跑相同的汗珠。

dict_mnemonic.note: 义项记忆 · 汗 → 出汗 → 辛苦
dict_mnemonic.text: sweat 是汗水，作动词指出汗，引申为辛苦劳动；注意与 sweet（甜的）只差一个字母。

root: 来自古英语 swat，源于日耳曼语 swaitaz，核心是身体受热或用力时渗出的液体。

sensesIntro.en: Sweat means the liquid from the skin, the act of producing it, or hard effort.
sensesIntro.cn: sweat 指皮肤渗出的液体、出汗的动作，或辛苦劳动。

core.en: Effort made visible on the skin.

branches.en: After the long run, he was covered in sweat.
branches.cn: 跑完长跑后，他满头是汗。

branches.en: The room was hot and sweat ran down his face.
branches.cn: 房间很热，汗水顺着他的脸流下。

branches.en: The runners were sweating in the sun.
branches.cn: 跑步者在太阳下出汗。

branches.en: She earned the prize with years of sweat.
branches.cn: 她多年辛苦才赢得这个奖。

branches.en: Drops on the skin and years of labor share one word.
branches.cn: 皮肤上的汗珠与多年的劳动共用一个词。

intro.en: Sweat forms sweaty, sweater, and compounds such as sweatband.
intro.cn: sweat 可构成 sweaty、sweater 以及 sweatband 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: Sweat is Germanic; the Latin perspirare gave perspire and perspiration.
latinIntro.cn: sweat 属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 perspirare 产生 perspire 与 perspiration。

latinEntries.example: Swat is the Old English source of sweat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: swat 是 sweat 的古英语来源。
